title: Practise The Skill, Session One
objective: Work on the skill you chose, keep the tool and the box the same, and record what changed between your first attempt and your last.

blocks.text: BUILD · Art · Week 2. Trinity Arts Award Bronze. Practise The Skill, Session One.
Objective: work on the skill you chose, keep the tool and the box the same, and record what changed between your first attempt and your last.
Success evidence: a strip with every box numbered, box one and your last box ringed, and one sentence that names the change.

Your skill came off a card in the approved skill pack. You talk about the mark, the tool and the box. You are never asked about your home, your family, your body or what you believe. Nobody in this room is asked what they believe. Identity here means what your own artwork keeps choosing, and it is read off the strip in front of you.
40 minutes. Offline.

This deck evidences Bronze Part A, Explore the arts as a participant. The register says Part A requires active participation in any art form, improvement, and a summary of what they learnt. Today's strip is the participation and the improvement record; the summary comes later in Part A. Bronze attempted rule, in the register's words: ONE Attempted allowed overall. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. The evidence file cap is 10 files for the whole Bronze level, so append the strip to the cumulative Part A file and label its page; do not open a new file for each session. The three assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, and communication.

Delivery is through a validated centre; confirm local validation and an adviser trained at Bronze before assessment. Neither is asserted as completed here. Core, Extend and Challenge are support routes inside Bronze, not different awards. The prompts and sample quantities are teaching scaffolds, not extra assessment requirements. Scribe only the pupil’s own words. Store evidence by part; one cumulative file per part is a suggested four-file plan within the ten-file cap.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve
stages.data-ta1: Skill strips and last week's measure flat on the desk before pupils sit. Use the tool chosen for the skill; keep it the same across these trials.
stages.data-ta2: If a pupil has no measure from last week, read them the spare measure card and start there. Do not stop to rebuild the whole sheet.

blocks.text: One attempt records a start
Last week you chose one art form skill.
You also wrote a measure for it.
A measure is the thing you can see or count.
Find that measure now and read it out.
Today you work on that same skill six times.
Each go is called an attempt.
One attempt records a starting point.
Two attempts can show a change.
They only show it if you can tell them apart.
So every attempt gets its own number today.
Measures out before the starter. A pupil practising without last week's measure will write a feeling at the end, and the record then has nothing to answer to.
You need your measure, a trial sheet and the safe tool for your chosen skill.

stages.title: Starter · create the need
stages.data-ta1: Draw both strips on the board yourself. Never use a pupil's page as the weak example.

blocks.text: Two strips, one skill
Watch two strips of practice.
The first strip has six boxes and no numbers.
I cannot tell you which box came first.
So I cannot say that anything changed.
The second strip has six numbered boxes.
I can hold box one next to box six.
Now the change is there to see.
The practice was the same. The record was not.

items: 1 · number every box before you start.
2 · keep the same tool all the way.
3 · keep every box the same size.
4 · stop and compare box one with your last.

blocks.text: Make the order clear so someone else can follow your practice.

stages.title: I Do · model
stages.data-ta1: Time the minute out loud and stop on it. Your stop is the rule they copy all lesson.
stages.data-ta2: If a pupil answers with home, family or what they believe, say: today we only talk about the mark and the box. Then point at their strip and move on. Do not comment.

blocks.text: I practise, and I keep the box the same
My skill is cross hatching in pencil.
My measure is that the lines stay even.
For cross hatching, draw a set of light lines with even gaps. Add a second set across them at an angle. Keep each set steady. More close lines make a darker patch; wider gaps leave it pale.
I number all six boxes before I draw.
I start in box one and work for one minute.
Then I stop, even if the box is not full.
Stopping keeps every box worth the same.
I move to box two and do it again.
Same pencil. Same box size. Same one minute.
Those three things stay locked all the way along.

blocks.caption: Four steps, and the last one is your evidence
blocks.title: Practising so the change can be read
blocks.alt: Boxes labelled NUMBER, PRACTISE, RING, COMPARE. Four steps, and the last one is your evidence

blocks.text: At the end I ring box one and box six.
I put those two side by side and look.
In box one my lines cross at odd angles.
In box six two sets of lines cross, with even gaps in each set.
The gaps between them are the same size.
That is my measure, so the change is real.
I write: by box six my lines are more even.
That names the mark and answers my measure.
Model the tool action and the stop. Similar trial times help comparison. If a trial runs longer, note that change and discuss what it may explain; keep the genuine record.

stages.title: We Do · predict then check
stages.data-ta1: Use the model activity, then transfer the idea to the learner’s own work. Allow speech, pointing or a scribe.

data.heading: Predict, then check a practice trial
data.instruction: These are made-up model trials. First predict. Check the model with your adult when you are ready. Your own result may differ.

items.label: The same soft pencil presses harder. What might change?
items.feedback: Model result: the marks got darker; the paper size stayed the same. Test what happens with your own pencil.

items.label: A fine pencil is swapped for thick chalk. What else might change?
items.feedback: Model result: the chalk marks were wider. A new tool can change more than one feature.

items.label: The tool, paper, time and box size stay the same. What do you predict we can compare?

options.label: The first and last marks fairly

items.feedback: Model check: these two boxes can be compared. They may show change or no clear change. Neither result proves what every artist will do.

data.discussion: Say which prediction the model supported. Keep the same tool and box size in your own practice. Record what really happens.
data.staffNote: Ask for predictions before opening explanations. The reported results belong to the labelled fictional trials. They are not guaranteed effects or evidence of pupil progress. Accept a reasoned different prediction, then discuss the supplied result.

stages.data-ta2: Ask for predictions before opening explanations. The reported results belong to the labelled fictional trials. They are not guaranteed effects or evidence of pupil progress. Accept a reasoned different prediction, then discuss the supplied result.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect
stages.data-ta1: Both strips up at once. Let the group say which one proves something before you tell them.

blocks.text: Change one thing, not three
Watch a trial where too much changes.
I use pencil in box one. In box six I use pen, twice the space and three minutes.
The last marks look stronger. Was it the pen, space or time? I cannot tell.
Keep your tool, box size and time the same. This makes practice easier to judge.
Read your measure before you compare. Name a change we can find: even gaps, straighter lines or darker marks.
“Better” needs a detail and a reason. Point to the mark that supports your view.

boxes.head: ONE THING CHANGES
boxes.line1: same pencil, same box, same minute
boxes.line2: easier to judge what practice changed

boxes.head: THREE THINGS CHANGE
boxes.line1: new pen, bigger box, longer go
boxes.line2: harder to tell what practice changed

blocks.caption: Like-sized trials make the change easier to explain
blocks.title: Locked conditions against loose ones
blocks.alt: Two practice records: a comparable pair makes it easier to judge what changed.

items: 2 · same box size all the way.
4 · compare box one with your last box.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab
stages.data-ta1: Keep the earlier model visible for this paired check. Pupils have not made their independent work yet; do not ask for a sheet that does not exist.
stages.data-ta2: A pupil who will not swap may run the three checks on their own strip while you read them aloud.

blocks.text: Check the strip, then check the words
Use the model practice strip shown earlier. Your own piece comes next.
Work in twos with the model strip.
Do not swap the tools used for the trials.
There are three checks and they go in order.
Check one is a number in every box.
If a box has no number, write miss beside it.
Check two is the same tool all the way.
Check three is boxes of the same size.
Put a tick on the strip if all three hold.
A tick means the strip can be compared.
Now one person names the change in the model out loud.
They must name the mark, not the mood.
If they say better, ask them which mark.
Then point at the two boxes they mean.
Then swap roles, with two minutes each way.

stages.title: Independent · evidence
stages.data-ta1: Prepare safe tools for each chosen skill. Model the relevant step: measure a small paint mix, turn card while cutting, or cross two sets of pencil lines. Keep test size and tool steady; record the pupil’s real result.
stages.data-ta2: A pupil who sees no change writes that, and rings the box they worked hardest in. No change is a real record, not a blank.

blocks.text: Six boxes, then one sentence

Practise the skill on your own card. For paint, repeat a small colour mix. For cutting, repeat the same edge with safe tools. For drawing, repeat the chosen marks. Label each test so you can compare the first and last.
Work on your own now.
Number your boxes one to six first.
Then work one minute in each box.
Stop when I call time, every single time.
Keep the same chosen tool and size to the last trial.
When the strip is full, ring box one.
Then ring your last box as well.
Hold the two ringed boxes side by side.
Read your measure again before you write.
Then write one sentence under the strip.
Start it with the words by box six.
Name the mark that changed, then say how.

items: Core · Make and number the practice boxes. Ring the first and last. Say what changed and have your words recorded.
Extend · as Core, and write one sentence starting by box six that names the mark that changed.
Challenge · as Extend, and name the box where the change first shows.

blocks.text: If you finish early, write the one thing you will keep the same next session.
No clear change yet is a real result too. Point at both trials and say what stayed the same. Never invent a change to fill the line.

stages.title: Exit · Audience and Influence
stages.data-ta1: The named adult reads the sentence back word for word, then points at the two ringed boxes. Acknowledge the choice, and keep the pupil’s words unchanged.

blocks.text: Say it once to an adult
Read your sentence to the adult at your table.
They read it back to you word for word.
Then they look at box one and your last box.
If no clear change shows, record no clear change yet.
One sentence is enough. Do not write more.
Now write today's date on the strip.
Write the sheet name and the page number too.
That is how anybody finds this strip again.
Now pick one thing that happens next. Keep the same measure, change nothing but the day, or add two more boxes.
Write your pick under your sentence.

Evidence locator, from the register: a locator names the file plus the page, slide or timecode, and "in arts log" is refused as a locator. So the sheet name and page number go on the strip today, before it is filed.
Add this work to your Part A file. Write the file name and page number. For a sound or video clip, give the file name and the time where your evidence starts.

checks: Every box on the strip carries its own number.
The same tool and the same box size run from box one to the last box.
